summary: Cobbler profiles and mgmt-classes become groups and ksmeta values become variables. Hosts are addressed by DNS name, so 'foo*' matches but 'foo' doesn't, and inventory script variables override same-named ones you pass.
questions: Why can't Ansible find my Cobbler host by short name?
How do Cobbler mgmt-classes map to Ansible groups?
Can I use Cobbler ksmeta values in templates?
Do Cobbler variables override my own variables?

answer_card.title: How Cobbler data maps to inventory
answer_card.answer_md:
- Cobbler profiles and `--mgmt-classes` become groups (for example `webserver`, `atlanta`).
- `--ksmeta` values become host variables usable in templates: `{{ a }}`, `{{ b }}`, `{{ c }}`.
- Hosts are reached by DNS name only, so `ansible foo` finds nothing but `ansible 'foo*'` matches `foo.example.com`.
- Variables from the inventory script override your variables with the same name.
